chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: The Cherry Blossom session where Prez cut Coleman Hawkins
summary: Lester Young outplayed Hawkins at a jam session, then was fired by Fletcher Henderson for his tone.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, I mean was Lester playing tenor then with that sort of light tone?
Yeah, he was playing that tenor with the alto style.
Well, did you like that?
Well, I did. But, you know, everybody was a Coleman Hawkins fan.
Right. That's what I mean.
And it was in '33 when we went over
there and saw that music ?, you know, when they needed somebody to take Hawk's place in Fletcher Henderson's band.
Right.
And this was at the Cherry Blossom. I slipped away from school that night. (chuckle)
(laughter) Yes.

I skipped away, and about four of us went over there. And we'd heard about the sessions coming in, you know, so we got there. There was Ben and Herschel and Dick Wilson, about three or four other of the local, you know, and Hawk. And, man, Hawk was cuttin' everybody out. Prez (phonetic) got 'em. And immediately became the talk of the town. Now Prez, after he tore Hawk apart, he tore Hawk up so bad, Hawk missed the date in St. Louis. Hawk was still trying to get him at 12 o'clock that night stand (phonetic)-- (chuckle) you know. Seemed like the longer Prez played, the longer they had that head-cuttin' session, and the better Prez got, you know.
Well, when you--was it sort of his originality of ideas, was it, that --?
More creative things, you know. You see, first you must remember that in Kansas City, the adage was--still is--'say somethin' on your horn.'
Yeah.
Not just show off your versatility and--
Right.
--ability to execute. Tell us a story, and don't let it be a lie. Let it mean something. If it's only one note, like Louis Armstrong, like Duke would do, you know, with that 'lu'?
Yeah. Well, but, you know, it's still surprising to me that he could've caught Hawk.
Tore Hawk up. Tore Hawk, Herschel and everybody else up, and then he got a job with Fletcher--
Right.
--and Fletcher fired him right away.
Well, he fired him--
--because of his tone.
Yeah.
Yeah. And everybody put him, like, you know, like came down--came on back to the wasn't too proud to come on back to Basie, you know.
